title: Lumora — SaaS Analytics Platform
description: End-to-end design of a real-time analytics dashboard for B2B marketing teams, built around clarity at scale.
challenge: Marketing teams drowned in noisy data across 12 disconnected tools. The existing dashboard had a 68% abandonment rate on key insights pages — users could not extract actionable signals from the visual noise.
solution: I consolidated the information architecture into three mental models: Overview, Drill-down, and Alert. A consistent token-based design system (600+ components) enabled the engineering team to ship at 3x their previous velocity. Key innovation: a 'Signal vs. Noise' view toggle that collapses secondary metrics with a single click.
results: Reduced time-to-insight from 14 minutes to 2.3 minutes (measured via session replay)
Dashboard abandonment dropped from 68% to 19%
Design system adopted by 4 additional product teams within 3 months

title: Vanta — Brand Identity & Web
description: Full brand identity and marketing website for a Series A cybersecurity startup — designed to project trust while staying approachable.
challenge: Cybersecurity brands default to cold blues and shield icons — visually indistinguishable in a crowded market. Vanta needed a visual identity that communicated rigorous security without the sterile enterprise aesthetic that repels SMB buyers.
solution: I developed an identity anchored in 'structured warmth': a muted amber palette (unusual for security), geometric precision in the mark, and a typographic system pairing a condensed display font with generous body spacing. The website uses large surface areas and intentional whitespace to create calm, counter-intuitively signaling thoroughness.
results: Brand recall doubled in user testing compared to previous identity
Website conversion rate increased 34% in the first 30 days post-launch
Featured in Fonts In Use and Awwwards nominee

title: Forma — Luxury E-Commerce Redesign
description: Full UX overhaul of a mid-market furniture brand's e-commerce experience, focused on the consideration-to-purchase funnel.
challenge: Cart abandonment sat at 81% — far above the 70% industry average. Research revealed that customers lacked material and finish confidence before committing to high-ticket items ($800–$4,000 range). Product pages felt generic, not premium.
solution: Redesigned the product detail page around material storytelling: full-bleed texture photography, a 'Build Your Room' configurator letting users mix finishes live, and an AR placement feature. Checkout was compressed from 7 steps to 3 with address autofill and persistent cart.
results: Cart abandonment reduced from 81% to 61%
Average order value increased 22% (mix-and-match bundles)
AR feature used in 38% of sessions — highest engagement touchpoint

title: Meridian — Travel Planning App
description: iOS travel planning app combining itinerary management with local discovery for independent travelers in emerging destinations.
challenge: Existing travel apps cater to either hyper-organized planners (rigid spreadsheet-like interfaces) or serendipitous explorers (discovery feeds with no structure). Solo travelers in less-documented destinations fell between both — they needed structure with flexibility.
solution: Designed a dual-mode interface: Plan mode (structured day-by-day itinerary with time blocks) and Explore mode (map-first, card-based discovery). The key innovation was a 'gravity' system — saving a discovery item automatically pulled it toward open time blocks in the itinerary, making planning feel effortless.
results: 4.8 App Store rating from 2,400 reviews in first 6 months
Day-7 retention of 41% (industry benchmark: 25%)
Featured by Apple in 'Apps We Love' editorial

title: Helix — Fintech Onboarding
description: Redesign of the onboarding flow for a neobank targeting freelancers — reducing KYC drop-off while meeting regulatory requirements.
challenge: KYC (Know Your Customer) onboarding in financial products is notoriously friction-heavy. Helix was losing 71% of signups during the verification step — a 40-screen flow that felt indistinguishable from a government form.
solution: I mapped all 40 screens to emotional states in user research, identifying that anxiety peaks at document upload and again at 'awaiting review'. The redesign introduced a visual progress metaphor (a timeline, not a step counter), split long waits with micro-wins (instant card reveal during verification), and rewrote all error messages in plain language.
results: KYC completion rate improved from 29% to 58%
Support tickets during onboarding dropped 44%
Regulatory review passed with zero accessibility violations

title: Grove — Digital Magazine
description: Art direction and web design for an independent digital magazine covering architecture, craft, and slow living.
challenge: Most editorial websites treat the web as a PDF renderer — fixed columns, predictable grids, no expressive use of the medium. Grove wanted to publish work that feels as considered as the subjects it covers, without sacrificing readability at scale.
solution: Built a modular editorial system where each issue gets a bespoke layout 'skin' (custom grid, color palette, and typographic scale) while sharing a common reading engine underneath. Longform articles use a variable font that subtly increases weight as users scroll deeper — a subtle reward for engagement.
results: Average reading time increased from 2:10 to 6:40 (3x improvement)
Subscriber conversion from free readers increased 18%
Won Communications Arts Interactive Award 2023

title: Atlas — Enterprise Design System
description: Built Atlas from scratch — a scalable design system serving 14 product teams across a 1,200-person enterprise software company.
challenge: Fourteen product teams, zero consistency. New features took 3+ weeks to design because every designer was rebuilding the same patterns. The existing 'design system' was a 3-year-old Sketch file no one trusted.
solution: Led a 6-month discovery phase (interviewing 40+ designers and engineers) before writing a single component. Prioritized ruthlessly: Atlas launched with 48 components covering 90% of use cases, not 200 covering everything. Pair programmed with engineering leads to ensure Figma tokens mapped 1:1 to CSS variables.
results: New feature design time reduced from 3 weeks to 4 days (average)
System adopted by all 14 teams within 8 months
Design-to-dev handoff errors dropped 76% in first quarter of adoption

title: Solstice — Wellness & Mindfulness
description: Meditation and sleep wellness app with personalized programs — designed to minimize cognitive load for users in distress.
challenge: Users open wellness apps when they're already overwhelmed. Existing apps paradoxically added cognitive load: too many choices, too much gamification, too many notifications. Users felt guilty for not using the app 'correctly'.
solution: Designed around three principles: one tap to start, no streaks or guilt mechanics, and ambient rather than alert-based nudges. The onboarding learns your schedule passively (via calendar permission) and surfaces the right session type at natural pause points in your day.
results: Week-4 retention rate of 52% vs 31% industry average
NPS of 74 (exceptional for wellness category)
App Store 'Editor's Choice' awarded at launch

title: Nomo — Restaurant Brand & Web
description: Brand identity and immersive website for a high-concept Tokyo-inspired omakase restaurant in New York.
challenge: High-end restaurants rely on word-of-mouth and editorial coverage — their web presence is typically an afterthought. Nomo needed a digital experience that justified its $180 prix-fixe price point before guests arrived.
solution: Designed a cinematic website experience: a dark, textured canvas that loads the menu as a slow-motion video essay rather than a static list. Each dish has a micro-documentary (30s) that plays on hover. Reservations are embedded without leaving the page. The brand identity borrows from Japanese packaging — minimal, precise, meaningful negative space.
results: Reservation wait list grew from 2 weeks to 3 months within 60 days of launch
Press coverage in The New York Times, Eater NY, and Bon Appétit
Website named in Awwwards 'Best Restaurant Sites of 2021'
